about: Radio and intercom for chapter 3: the approach, lunar orbit insertion behind the Moon, Earthrise, the first orbits, descent orbit insertion and the first low pass. t = GET (seconds from liftoff), timed to lunar-space.js (loss of signal 88:49:46, LOI 88:54:22, AOS 89:25:16, DOI 93:08:22, AOS 93:45:46, low point 94:05:19). Original lines in the style of Apollo procedure; not quotes.

lines.text: There she is, out the left window. She grows every time I look.
Apollo, Houston. Your trajectory is right on. Midcourse correction four is not required.
I could watch this all day. The terminator, and the craters along it. Every hour there is more of it.
Good morning, Apollo. This is lunar orbit day. We have your burn data whenever you are ready to copy.
Ready to copy, Houston. Go ahead.
It fills the whole window now. That is not a picture any more. It is a place.
Apollo, Houston. You are go for lunar orbit insertion.
Roger, go for LOI. Thank you, Houston.
Apollo, Houston. Two minutes to loss of signal. All your systems look good. We'll see you on the other side.
See you on the other side, Houston.
Turning round for the burn. Engine first.
And that's it. No more Houston. Just the three of us, and the far side.
One minute. Engine armed.
Ignition.
Thrust is good. You can feel it push you into the couch.
Three minutes. Chamber pressure is steady.
Shutdown.
Three fifteen by ninety seven kilometres. We are in lunar orbit.
Welcome to the Moon, gentlemen.
Earthrise! Out your window. There she comes, over the edge.
Apollo, Houston. Standing by for your burn report.
Houston, Apollo. The burn went right on time. Three fifteen by ninety seven. And the view, Houston. You would not believe the view.
We copy, Apollo. Good burn. Welcome to lunar orbit.
The whole Earth, coming up over a horizon that isn't ours.
Coming up on Taurus-Littrow. Look for the valley between the two big massifs.
There. The North Massif, the South Massif, and the valley floor between them. That is where we are going.
Apollo, Houston. Two minutes to loss of signal. See you on the other side.
Apollo, Houston. We have looked at your numbers. You are go for descent orbit insertion.
Roger, go for DOI.
Apollo, Houston. Two minutes to loss of signal. Go for DOI. See you on the other side.
One minute to DOI.
Ignition.
Shutdown. Twenty two seconds, right on the money.
Fifteen kilometres at the low point. Ninety seven at the high.
Houston, Apollo. DOI was good. We are in the descent orbit.
Roger, Apollo. We confirm. It looks good from here.
We are coming down low. Look how fast it goes by now.
Fifteen kilometres. Every crater has its own shadow.
There is the valley. Tomorrow we will be standing down there.
Apollo, Houston. That is a beautiful orbit. Time for some rest. Big day tomorrow.
Copy, Houston. Good night.
